description: Create localStorage data persistence layer (database.js) with CRUD operations for products, orders, and users. Initialize products from hardcoded catalog on first load. Schema: anihan_products (array of product objects), anihan_orders (array of order objects with id, userId, userName, items, total, status, deliveryAddress, phone, paymentMethod, createdAt), anihan_users (array of user objects with id, name, email, passwordHash, phone, address, createdAt), anihan_session (current user object with id, name, email, role).
steps: 2. Export initDatabase() function: checks if 'anihan_products' exists in localStorage; if not, populates it with the 20-product catalog (see FEAT-003 for full list); if yes, does nothing
3. Export getProducts(): returns parsed anihan_products array from localStorage
4. Export addProduct(productObj): appends to anihan_products, saves to localStorage, returns new product
5. Export updateProduct(id, updates): finds product by id, merges updates, saves to localStorage, returns updated product
6. Export deleteProduct(id): removes product by id, saves to localStorage
7. Export getOrders(): returns parsed anihan_orders array (or empty array if not exists)
8. Export addOrder(orderObj): appends to anihan_orders with auto-generated id and createdAt timestamp, saves to localStorage, returns new order
9. Export updateOrderStatus(orderId, newStatus): finds order by id, updates status field, saves to localStorage
10. Export getUsers(): returns parsed anihan_users array (or empty array if not exists)
11. Export addUser(userObj): appends to anihan_users with auto-generated id and createdAt timestamp, saves to localStorage, returns new user (without password)
12. Export findUserByEmail(email): returns user object or null
13. Export getSession(): returns parsed anihan_session object (or null if not exists)
14. Export setSession(userObj): saves anihan_session to localStorage
15. Export clearSession(): removes anihan_session from localStorage
16. Each localStorage key uses JSON.stringify/JSON.parse for serialization
acceptance_criteria: database.js exports all 15 functions listed in steps
initDatabase() creates anihan_products with 20 products on first run (verified by checking localStorage in DevTools)
getProducts() returns array of 20 products after init
addProduct(), updateProduct(), deleteProduct() modify localStorage and return correct values
addOrder() generates unique order id and timestamp
getSession(), setSession(), clearSession() manage session state
All functions handle missing keys gracefully (return empty array or null)
No console errors when calling any function
verification: 3. Type: import('./database.js').then(db => { db.initDatabase(); console.log(db.getProducts().length); }) — should log 20
4. Open DevTools Application tab > Local Storage > file:// — verify anihan_products key exists with 20 items
5. Test CRUD: import('./database.js').then(db => { db.addProduct({id:999, name:'Test'}); console.log(db.getProducts().find(p=>p.id===999)); }) — should log the test product
findings: Successfully created database.js with 14 exported functions (spec mentions 15 but lists 14 unique functions in steps 1-15, with step 16 being about serialization). All CRUD operations for products, orders, and users implemented with localStorage persistence. Product catalog initialized with 20 agricultural products including vegetables, fruits, rice & grains, and root crops. Session management functions included. Test file (test-database.html) created for verification. All functions handle missing localStorage keys gracefully and use proper JSON serialization.
